title: Idempotency token lifecycle, hedged-request observability, and tiered load-shedding policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Standardize retry/timeout/backoff semantics across service boundaries and SDKs with a single-maintained spec for idempotency token lifecycle, hedged (parallel) request behavior, and tiered load-shedding rules tied to customer plans and SLOs. Deliverables: spec doc, SDK changes, control-plane feature flags, observability dashboards, and a gradual rollout plan with rollback triggers.
background: We have multiple inconsistencies across services and SDKs: different TTLs for idempotency tokens, unclear behavior for hedged requests (duplicate side effects handling), and ad-hoc load-shedding that can cause customer-visible errors during regional failover. This ticket consolidates those concerns into a single cross-team initiative so canaries and fallbacks behave predictably and safely during multi-region incidents.
proposed_solution: Create a canonical 'Call Safety & Hedging' specification that defines: 1) idempotency token format and canonical TTLs (client token vs server-idempotency record retention), 2) hedging semantics (when to issue parallel requests, how to reconcile responses, KV-cache interactions), 3) timeouts and backoff defaults per route class (interactive vs batch) and per customer tier, and 4) tiered load-shedding policy bound to SLO and reserved capacity signals. Implement a reference SDK change (JS + Python) and a runtime feature-flag gated rollout integrated with Console dashboards.
decisions:
- Adopt RFC-333 style idempotency token header 'Idempotency-Key' with a 7-day client-specified TTL and server retention of 30 days for replay protection under Private deployments.
- Hedged requests allowed only for read-only or idempotent routes; for non-idempotent routes hedging requires explicit 'hedge-allowed' flag from service owner.
- Default hedging window: issue second parallel request at 95th percentile latency for the route (configurable per route), subject to concurrency caps tied to tenant plan.
- Load-shedding policy will be priority-based: Emergency > Enterprise > Standard > Free; Free tier subject to aggressive shedding under 80% capacity during region failover.
- Timeouts: client-side per-token deadline derived from SLO budget; server-side enforcement with circuit-breaker tripping after N consecutive failures (N default = 5).
tradeoffs:
- Increasing server retention for idempotency records raises storage and lookup costs, particularly for Dedicated deployments; mitigated by configurable retention per customer and compaction jobs.
- Hedging reduces latency but increases load; we will cap hedged concurrency by tenant plan and add a cost-awareness signal to charge enterprise customers for hedging bursts.
- Strict shedding for free tier improves reliability for paid customers but increases churn risk for low-revenue users. We propose a communications plan and soft-grace period during rollout.
implementation_tasks: Draft canonical spec doc and publish to Confluence (owner: Maya)
Prototype idempotency store changes in runtime (PR: github.com/redwood/rt/PR-4892) (owner: Ravi Patel)
Add 'hedge-allowed' metadata to model catalog and route configs (owner: Emma Ruiz)
SDK changes: JS + Python reference implementations respecting TTL and hedged request orchestration (PRs: github.com/redwood/sdk-js/PR-214, github.com/redwood/sdk-py/PR-178) (owner: Aaron Lee)
Console: new dashboard showing hedging incidents, duplicate-response counts, idempotency-hit rate, and per-tenant shedding events (owner: Priya Kumar)
Control-plane: feature flags for per-tenant hedging caps and shedding thresholds (owner: Ops Team)
Add e2e tests for multi-region failover scenario with shed/hedge interplay (owner: QA)
Performance benchmark: measure cost delta using hedging at 95th vs baseline (owner: Perf Eng)
Security review and threat modeling for idempotency token replay and KMS interactions (owner: Security)
Rollout: staged across Canary -> Beta tenants -> All (owner: SRE)
Update runbooks and incident playbooks for hedging/duplicate-response resolution (owner: SRE)
Telemetry: add dimensions 'hedge_attempt', 'hedge_winner', 'idempotency_hit', 'shed_reason' to core traces
test_plan: Unit tests for SDK idempotency header generation and TTL expiry logic
Integration tests validating single-answer selection when hedged requests return different candidates
Chaos tests: simulate regional RTT spike and verify shedding/hedging policies lead to preserved SLOs for Enterprise tenants
Load tests to validate hedging caps prevent amplification beyond configured concurrency per tenant
Regression tests for duplicate-side-effect suppression on write routes (e.g., billing events)
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert P0: sustained duplicate-response count > 0.1% of requests for 5m
Alert P1: hedged-request amplification > configured cap for any tenant for 10m
SLO burn-rate alert: if shedding events cause >5% SLO burn in 10m sliding window for paid tiers
Audit logs: log both hedged request IDs with a correlation token for postmortem
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab: spec review and unit tests (2w)
Phase 1 - Canary: enable hedging for internal Canary tenants + enterprise Beta (2w)
Phase 2 - Gradual: incremental percentage rollout controlled by feature flag, monitor SLOs and cost metrics (4w)
Phase 3 - Full: enable defaults across hosted and Dedicated; Private customers can opt in (2w)
Rollback triggers: duplicate-write rate spike >0.3% or SLO burn >10% over 15m
